summary: This work develops a closed-loop calibration workflow combining echoed leakage error amplification (ELEA) and context-aware fidelity estimation (CAFE) circuits to achieve CZ gate fidelity exceeding $99.9\%$ on an 84-qubit superconducting processor with tunable transmon qubits and couplers. Automated recalibration every 0.5 hours maintains gate stability over 9-hour monitoring periods, with median fidelity $99.25\%$ across 72 parallel CZ gates and coherent error suppressed to $0.007\%$.
motivation: Scalable superconducting processors suffer from increased incoherent errors due to TLS defects and crosstalk from high control-line density, leaving reduced tolerance for coherent calibration errors. Achieving CZ fidelities near the $0.1\%$ error threshold for fault-tolerant quantum error correction on multi-qubit processors requires precise parameter tuning and automated stabilization.
method: A three-stage calibration workflow iteratively applies SEA (for Z-interaction tuning), ELEA (for leakage suppression to state $|02\rangle$), and CAFE (fine amplitude and phase calibration) circuits. Flux pulse amplitudes $A_1, A_2, A_c$ are optimized using hyperbolic pulse shaping with $\eta=10$, $T=48$ ns gate duration, and virtual $Z$ phases compensate single-qubit errors. Automated recalibration repeats the fine CAFE stage every 0.5 hours to track environmental drift.
result: Maximum single-pair CZ fidelity reached $(99.92 \pm 0.01)\%$ with incoherent error $0.079\%$ and coherent error $0.007\%$, and leakage error $< 0.001\%$; median fidelity across 72 gates was $(99.25 \pm 0.01)\%$ with median error rate $0.75\%$. Automated calibration reduced error rate drift significantly in high-fluctuation qubits (e.g., Q$69$, Q$62$) over 9-hour periods compared to calibration-free control, with median single-qubit error $0.05\%$ (randomized benchmarking, $14$ ns pulses with DRAG).
